title: TG-300 Telemetry Gateway

headings.text: 5.1 No readings arrive at the broker

key_sentences: The TG-300 collects readings from field sensors over Modbus RTU and forwards them to a central broker over MQTT.
It is written for installers who are familiar with basic Linux commands.
You only need a laptop with an SSH client and a web browser to complete the set-up.
An interrupted update leaves the gateway in recovery mode and requires a site visit.
All settings are kept in a single YAML file at /etc/tg300/gateway.yaml.
Check that the collector service is running and that the broker host name resolves from the gateway.
Timeouts usually come from a wrong baud rate or from a missing terminating resistor.
For further help, contact the support desk and quote the serial number printed on the side of the unit.

list_items.text: Mount the gateway on a DIN rail inside the enclosure, away from frequency converters.
Connect the RS-485 line to terminals A and B.
Use a 120 ohm terminating resistor at the last device.
Keep the cable shield grounded at one end only.
Connect the Ethernet cable and apply power; the status LED blinks green while the system starts.
Log in over SSH with the installer account printed on the label inside the lid.

code:
sudo tg-update --channel stable
sudo systemctl enable --now tg-collector.service
systemctl status tg-collector.service --no-pager

site:
  id: PUMP-STATION-07
  timezone: Europe/Lisbon
modbus:
  port: /dev/ttyS1
  baudrate: 19200
  parity: even
  poll_interval_s: 15
mqtt:
  host: broker.example.net
  port: 8883
  tls: true
  topic_prefix: utilities/water/pumps
